statement_3.text: Collecting firewood for cooking is a chore that boys and girls should do together.

statement_5.text: If a girl misses school to herd animals or do chores I will speak up to get her back to class.

featured_stories.situation_before: Before the NutriBus came, I woke up at 5:00 AM every single morning to fetch three heavy jerrycans of water from the far borehole while my brother stayed asleep. By the time I carried firewood and swept, it was 9:30 AM. I was exhausted, reached school in tears, and missed all morning English and Math lessons. We only ate plain posho with salt at night.
featured_stories.campaign_event: NutriBus Day Session (Adere build, food sorting, or chore debate)
featured_stories.what_done_differently: Reallocated morning chores (boys fetching water/wood; girls arrived on time)
featured_stories.actual_words_done_differently: My brother Lokol now fetches two jerrycans of water with me every morning. We finish early, eat together, and walk together to school on time.
featured_stories.why_significant: Because I am no longer beaten or embarrassed for latecoming, I can concentrate without sleeping in class, and my midterm score improved from 42% to 78%. I feel respected at home and in class.
featured_stories.physical_evidence: School register shows consistent female attendance
featured_stories.collector_notes: Verified 100% on-time morning presence in Primary 6 register over 3 consecutive weeks without single recorded absence.

featured_stories.situation_before: I used to believe fetching water and gathering firewood was purely girls work. I would sit under the shade with other boys playing while my sisters struggled. My cousin had also dropped out of Primary 4 to herd cattle full time in the bush.
featured_stories.campaign_event: NutriBus Day Session (Adere build, food sorting, or chore debate)
featured_stories.actual_words_done_differently: I tracked my cousin in the kraal and convinced my uncle to re-enroll her in school. I also carry morning firewood and water alongside my sisters so we finish fast.
featured_stories.why_significant: I learned on NutriBus Day that when chores are shared equally, everyone succeeds. My cousin is now back in Primary 4 sitting right next to me, and my sisters are never late for morning assembly.
featured_stories.physical_evidence: School register shows consistent female attendance
featured_stories.collector_notes: Headteacher confirmed official re-enrollment and verified boys daily shared chore responsibility log.

featured_stories.situation_before: We only cooked plain white posho or thin maize porridge without any oil or greens. My two-year-old child was constantly lethargic, sickly, and underweight. Gathering firewood took 4 hours every single day using an open three-stone fire that burned through entire bundles in one morning.
featured_stories.campaign_event: Metu Porridge Plus Demonstration (Fortifying porridge with local staples)
featured_stories.what_done_differently: Supplemented Metu porridge with obtainable local wild greens or cowpeas
featured_stories.actual_words_done_differently: I began fortifying our daily Metu porridge with crushed roasted sesame and steamed cowpea leaves. We also constructed an improved double-pot mud stove using dry clay.
featured_stories.why_significant: My child gained healthy weight and vitality; her skin cleared up and she plays actively without crying. Plus I spend only 1 hour gathering wood instead of walking half the day into unsafe bush areas.
featured_stories.physical_evidence: Cooking pot shows Metu fortified with obtainable local greens
featured_stories.collector_notes: Collector inspected morning cooking pot: Metu porridge visibly fortified with dark-green steamed cowpea puree and roasted sesame paste.

featured_stories.situation_before: In our clan tradition, men and boys do not touch cooking pots or carry water. All firewood and water collection fell upon my wife and daughters. The youngest children always ate last from whatever little remained at the bottom of the bowl.
featured_stories.what_done_differently: Reallocated morning chores (boys fetching water/wood; girls arrived on time)
featured_stories.actual_words_done_differently: I told my sons that gathering firewood and water is family work, not just girls work. I built an improved sheltered mud cookstove for the manyatta and made sure the 3-year-old toddler is served first.
featured_stories.why_significant: I realized that our daughters education and our young childrens health are the real wealth of our family. An educated daughter brings prosperity and honor. My household is peaceful and united.
featured_stories.physical_evidence: Kitchen displays improved cookstove using less firewood
featured_stories.collector_notes: Collector verified newly constructed double-pot sheltered mud stove and observed youngest toddler served first during mealtime.

dimensions.title: Boys Helping with Morning Chores & Girls Arriving on Time
dimensions.summary: Morning girl absences dropped by 34% across monitored schools as boys took on morning borehole water and firewood collection.
dimensions.metric_label: Homes where boys share morning chores fairly
evidence_points: 90.5% of surveyed boys agreed that brothers and sisters should share morning chores equally.
Girls arriving at school on time jumped from 62% before to 94% after the campaign.
18 girls who had dropped out of school returned to class after fellow pupils visited them.

dimensions.title: Adding Local Green Vegetables to Morning Porridge
dimensions.summary: All 640 community demonstrations showed how to enrich daily porridge with easy-to-find local greens (Eboo, Lokaka) and cowpeas.
dimensions.metric_label: Mothers adding local greens to morning porridge
evidence_points: 1,586 Home Charts were returned signed by parents (86.2% return rate).
89.0% of returned charts showed mothers and fathers agreeing to cook green leaves daily.
100% local foods: zero expensive or unavailable food was promoted.

dimensions.title: Saving Firewood with Covered Pots & Better Stoves
dimensions.summary: Families cut firewood use by covering boiling pots and using simple improved cookstoves instead of open three-stone fires.
evidence_points: School kitchens moved away from smoky open three-stone fires to covered cooking.
Mothers reported firewood gathering dropped from 4 days a week to 2 days, saving time.
Less smoke in the kitchen led to fewer coughing complaints reported by health teams.

dimensions.title: Serving Toddlers and Young Children First
dimensions.summary: 82% of families changed the way they dish meals so that the youngest toddler is served a full bowl first before adults eat.
dimensions.metric_label: Homes that dish meals for the youngest child first
evidence_points: Village talks broke the old habit of small children eating only leftovers.
Fathers and elder leaders publicly agreed that children under two eat first.
The WFP toll-free hotline (0800) was announced at every gathering with zero complaints.

dimensions.title: Welcoming Children & Adults with Disabilities
dimensions.summary: 248 children and adults with disabilities took part as club members, village health workers, and cooking demonstration helpers.
evidence_points: 36 village health workers with disabilities mobilized their communities.
146 children with disabilities joined tactile food-sorting games and club meetings.
All 640 community demonstrations provided translated local language and accessible seating.

dimensions.title: Schools Continuing NutriClubs on Their Own
dimensions.summary: All 64 primary schools have signed joint calendars, active teacher patrons, and regular weekly morning assembly talks.
dimensions.metric_label: Schools with active weekly clubs & assembly talks
evidence_points: 128 teachers appointed as club patrons (2 per school) with Headteacher support.
Morning assembly talks held every week on Monday and Friday mornings.
Schools and village health workers continue joint weekly follow-ups.

how_much.headline: 640 Demos · 1,840 Home Charts
data_points: 640 community cooking demonstrations held across 64 school communities (10 per school community)
1,840 Home Charts given to pupils to take home to parents
All 64 schools practiced healthy food sorting and porridge enrichment

how_well.headline: 88.3% Cooked Hands-On · 100% Local Greens
data_points: 88.3% of caregivers cooked hands-on rather than just watching
100% compliance with easy-to-find wild greens (Eboo, Lokaka, cowpeas)
91.4% of children could clearly explain the food substitution rules

what_changed.headline: 84% Enrich Porridge · 82% Dish Toddlers First
data_points: Adding greens to porridge jumped from 12.0% before to 84.0% (+72.0% shift)
1,586 returned home charts confirmed daily green vegetables cooked at home
82.0% of families now dish food for the youngest toddler first (up from 22.0%)

how_much.headline: 64 Schools · 192 Visits · 128 Meetings
data_points: 64 primary schools completed all 3 visits (192 total visits)
64 active school clubs established with 3,280 member pupils
64 whole-school morning assembly talks delivered

how_well.headline: 92.2% Run by Teachers · 95.5% Attendance
data_points: 92.2% of schools delivered sessions independently without the visiting team
95.5% average attendance maintained across weekly club meetings
38 pupils with disabilities actively taking part in club activities

what_changed.headline: +8.7% Attendance · 94% Girls on Time
data_points: Overall school attendance grew from 3,350 to 3,640 pupils (+8.7% gain)
Girls on-time arrival rose from 62.0% to 94.0% (+32.0% punctuality gain)
18 girls who had dropped out were traced and brought back to class

how_much.headline: 640 Community Talks · 1,480 Fathers & Elders
data_points: 640 community discussions held in villages around all 64 schools (10 per school community)
1,480 fathers and elders actively took part in discussions
All 64 schools held the fair chore sharing debate

how_well.headline: 100% Peaceful Agreement · 90.5% Boys Affirm
data_points: 100% of village talks reached consensus without blaming any individual
Men actively tasted enriched porridge and joined stove demonstrations
90.5% of surveyed boys agreed domestic work belongs to brothers and sisters alike

what_changed.headline: 85% Share Chores Fairly · -34% Girl Absences
data_points: Boys sharing morning chores jumped from 18.0% to 85.0% (+67.0% shift)
Morning girl absences dropped by 34% as boys took on borehole water trips
Village elders formally agreed that boys carry water and toddlers eat first

monitoring_cycle_results.title: Where We Started (Baseline)
monitoring_cycle_results.desc: Checking the situation in sample schools before the campaign began
data_collected: Attendance: 3,350 pupils counted in school registers (1,630 girls, 1,720 boys)
Enriched Porridge: Only 12.0% of homes adding greens to porridge
Sharing Chores: Only 18.0% of boys helping with morning water or firewood
Serving Children First: Only 22.0% of families dishing the youngest child first

monitoring_cycle_results.title: Visit One: Getting Started in Class
monitoring_cycle_results.desc: Healthy food sorting, the Adere calabash game, and Home Charts given out
data_collected: Children Reached: 31,240 learners engaged across 64 schools
Classroom Practice: 100% of schools did the hands-on food sorting game
Home Charts Given: 1,840 Home Charts given to pupils to take to parents
Patrons Appointed: 128 teacher patrons confirmed by Headteachers

monitoring_cycle_results.title: NutriBus Day: School & Village Event
monitoring_cycle_results.desc: Big interactive bus stations, school pledges, and community cooking demos
data_collected: Attendance Growth: 3,510 pupils (+4.8% increase over baseline)
What Pupils Remembered: 91.4% of children remembered all 3 core messages
School Pledges: All 64 schools signed and hung up their commitment boards
Village Cooking Demos: 640 demonstrations underway (88.3% cooked hands-on)

monitoring_cycle_results.title: Visit Three: Checking Real Changes
monitoring_cycle_results.desc: Checking returned Home Charts, pupil teach-back, and ongoing clubs
data_collected: Attendance Growth: 3,640 pupils (+8.7% cumulative gain over baseline)
Charts Returned: 1,586 Home Charts brought back from parents (86.2% return rate)
School Commitments: 93.8% of school action plans verified actively working
Club Continuity: All 64 school clubs established ongoing weekly schedules

monitoring_cycle_results.title: In the Villages: Fathers, Elders & Stoves
monitoring_cycle_results.desc: Village gatherings, male participation, and saving firewood
data_collected: Community Demos: 640 cooking demonstrations held (10 per school community)
Elders & Fathers: 1,480 male elders joined talks on fair meals and chores
Home Follow-Up: 85% of visited homes confirmed boys fetching morning water
Hotline Redress: 0 complaints of unfair treatment on the WFP toll-free hotline

monitoring_cycle_results.title: On the Radio & For Everyone
monitoring_cycle_results.desc: Radio broadcasts, local language, and including people with disabilities
data_collected: Radio Broadcasts: 144 spots aired on Voice of Karamoja, Nenah FM, and Radio Pacis
Disability Inclusion: 248 people with disabilities took part in all activities
Local Language: 100% of talks and cards delivered in Ngakarimojong
Saving Firewood: 83.3% of homes saving wood with pot lids and better stoves
